questions.question: Why do LLM output tokens typically cost 3-4x more than input tokens?
options: Output tokens use a different, more expensive model
Generation is autoregressive — each output token requires a full forward pass
Output tokens are stored in a more expensive database
Output tokens consume more network bandwidth
questions.explanation: Input tokens are processed in parallel (a single forward pass), while output tokens are generated sequentially — each token requires its own forward pass. This per-token computation makes generation significantly more expensive.

questions.question: What is semantic caching in the context of LLM operations?
options: Caching model weights in GPU memory for faster inference
Storing previous LLM responses and returning them when a semantically similar query is received
Caching vector embeddings for faster retrieval
Pre-computing prompts to reduce latency
questions.explanation: Semantic caching stores query-response pairs and uses embedding similarity to match new queries against cached ones. If a new query is semantically similar to a cached query (e.g., cosine similarity > 0.95), the cached response is returned — avoiding an API call entirely.

questions.question: What is model routing for cost optimization?
options: Distributing traffic across multiple cloud regions
Directing simple queries to cheap models and complex queries to expensive models
Switching between different API providers based on availability
Routing requests to the nearest data center
questions.explanation: Model routing classifies incoming queries by complexity and routes simple tasks (classification, extraction) to cheap models (GPT-4o mini) and complex tasks (multi-step reasoning) to powerful models (GPT-4o). This can reduce costs by 10-16x.

questions.question: What does LangSmith tracing help with in LLM operations?
options: Automatically fixing bugs in LLM outputs
Debugging chains, tracking costs, and detecting regressions across LLM pipeline runs
Training new models on production data
Generating test cases for LLM applications
questions.explanation: LangSmith provides end-to-end tracing of LLM pipeline runs — showing each step's input, output, latency, and token usage. This enables cost attribution (which steps are expensive?), debugging (where did it go wrong?), and regression detection (is quality degrading?).

questions.question: What is prompt compression and how much can it typically reduce costs?
options: Removing all whitespace from prompts; reduces costs by 5%
Removing redundant context and instructions while preserving meaning; reduces tokens by 30-70%
Converting prompts to a binary format; reduces costs by 90%
Using shorter variable names in code prompts; reduces costs by 10%
questions.explanation: Prompt compression removes redundant instructions, context, and formatting while preserving the semantic content the model needs. Techniques include removing verbose system prompts, summarizing repeated context, and using concise formatting — typically achieving 30-70% token reduction with zero quality loss.
